You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Treasury Options Shift to Pricing in 2027 Rate Cuts; September Hike Expectations Cool Sharply; AI Industry Chain Under Broad Pressure (August 19, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Treasury options shift to pricing in 2027 rate cuts; September hike expectations cool markedly
After weaker July inflation, retail sales and consumer confidence data, coupled with an unexpected 23,000 decline in non-farm payrolls, interest-rate options markets began positioning for a potential Fed policy reversal.
Investors bought September-expiry options betting on a hold, while also accumulating March and June 2027 SOFR call options.
The probability of a September hike has dropped from a recent peak of about 68% two weeks ago to roughly half; interest-rate swaps now imply only about 9 basis points of tightening at the September meeting. Market Impact : Repricing of the policy path eases some tightening concerns, yet long-term yields remain elevated. The divergence between short-end and long-end expectations is creating differentiated pressure on growth stocks.
International Commodities
Trump pauses contact with Iran; geopolitical stalemate continues
A U.S. official said President Trump has instructed the negotiation team (including Vice President Vance, special envoy Witkoff and Kushner) to suspend contact with Iran.
White House strategy has shifted from “strike hard and fast” toward a longer-term approach of “choking Iran’s throat,” following earlier positive discussions. Market Impact : Suspension of Hormuz-related talks heightens supply uncertainty, providing geopolitical support for oil prices and prolonging sticky-inflation concerns.
Macroeconomic Policy
Multiple U.S. states tighten data-center power regulations; AI infrastructure becomes a midterm election issue
Pennsylvania requires data-center developers to secure their own power supply and raise clean-energy usage ratios; Texas has launched grid-connection audits; New York has paused new large-scale data centers.
Bank of America strategists list data-center regulation as a midterm-election variable; tighter rules could affect the pace of AI capital expenditure. Market Impact : Power and community constraints raise the cost and uncertainty of AI infrastructure deployment, drawing attention to related equipment and power suppliers while pressuring tech-hardware valuations.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,343/oz, +0.2%
Spot Silver : Approx. $63/oz, -0.52%
WTI Crude : Approx. $85/bbl, +0.87%
Brent Crude : Approx. $89/bbl, +0.56%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approx. 99.645, little changed
Driver Analysis : Trump’s pause in contact with Iran prolongs Hormuz uncertainty and supports oil prices. Gold is oscillating between rising rate-cut expectations and elevated long-term yields, while silver shows mixed industrial and safe-haven influences. Treasury options indicate a sharp drop in September hike odds, yet the 30-year yield remains high, limiting precious-metal upside. Institutional views hold that near-term commodities are jointly driven by geopolitics and interest-rate path repricing; elevated oil prices may reinforce the sticky-inflation narrative, creating a linkage of geopolitical stalemate → oil support → inflation expectations → policy-path reassessment.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $64,600, +0.31%
ETH : $1,915, +0.32%
Crypto Total Market Cap : $2.29 trillion, +0.2%
Market Liquidations : 24h total liquidations $205 million, of which long liquidations $119 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Current BTC price around $64,538. Dense high-leverage (50x/100x) short liquidation clusters sit in the $65,000–$66,000 zone above; a break higher could trigger successive short covering and amplify upside momentum. Long liquidation pressure in the $63,000–$64,000 area below has been partially released, with short-term leverage focus clearly skewed upward.
Spot ETF Net Flows : Yesterday net inflow of $298 million; current dynamic net inflow $46 million
Driver Analysis : The pullback in U.S. AI stocks and elevated long-term yields have dampened risk appetite, leaving crypto in a range-bound mode. Whales have net accumulated approximately 43,000 BTC over the past 60 days, indicating continued medium- to long-term buying on dips. ETF flow volatility coexists with leverage liquidations; institutional consensus points to range-bound trading, with attention on interest-rate path repricing and geopolitical developments for risk-asset transmission.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,343.40, -0.22%
SP 500 : Closed at 7,691.76, -0.69%

Tech Giants Dynamics

[...]
Performance Summary Driver Analysis : The Mag 7 showed clear divergence. Apple, Microsoft and Google were relatively resilient or higher, while Nvidia and Meta led the declines. AI hardware and semiconductor names came under significant valuation and regulatory pressure, prompting partial rotation into software and defensive sectors. Treasury options signal earlier rate-cut expectations, yet elevated long-end yields and tighter data-center regulations jointly weigh on high-capex growth stocks, producing differentiated individual-stock drivers.
[...]
5. Apple (AAPL) – Closed Higher Against the Tech Sell-Off
[...]
Event Overview : Apple rose approximately 1.45%, showing relative strength while the Nasdaq fell sharply and AI hardware sold off broadly; it was one of the few Mag 7 names to finish higher. Market Interpretation : Institutions view Apple as a relatively defensive tech allocation; the hardware cycle and services business provide a buffer, drawing flows when high-valuation AI hardware is sold. Investment Implications : Suitable as a steadier exposure within the tech sector; monitor new-product cycles and AI-feature adoption for longer-term growth contribution.
[...]
Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya, using a free-cash-flow sum-of-the-parts valuation, estimates Nvidia’s current share price trades at a 34%–50% discount to fair value even after incorporating ecosystem-financing risks. He argues the market may be overestimating Nvidia’s AI-investment risk, creating an “attractive buying opportunity.” Nvidia has committed roughly $300 billion in funding to projects such as OpenAI’s Ohio data-center campus and ecosystem partners (about $70 billion equity and $230 billion in residual-value guarantees or repurchase commitments). BofA maintains a Buy rating and $350 price target on Nvidia.
